Based on the context of your query, it looks like you are referring to "Pinion", a specific university capstone project developed by students at the University of Washington Information School. 
University of Washington Information School
What is the Pinion Capstone Project?
Created as a final group project by student developers and designers, Pinion is a digital platform designed to combat political apathy and help citizens ensure that elected officials are voting in their constituents' best interests. 
University of Washington Information School
The Core Problem: The project was built in response to data showing that 79% of people believe Congress prioritizes special interests over regular voters. 
University of Washington Information School
Features: It allows users to share political beliefs, track how local and national officials are voting, and compare personal stances to the collective "community opinion". 
University of Washington Information School
The Team: The platform was built by Marissa Exelby (Project Manager), Zach Holle (Backend Developer), Austin Hutchinson (Frontend Developer), and Henry Zhang (UX Designer). 
University of Washington Information School
Other Meanings (Mechanical & Bike Tech)
If your query was actually a mix of mechanical terms rather than the specific student project, it is worth noting that a pinion is fundamentally a small round gear used in drivetrain systems. In a structural or literal sense, a "capstone" is a crowning structural piece, but in engineering, a pinion interacts with larger gears or racks to drive motion. Additionally, Pinion is a well-known commercial brand that manufactures advanced bicycle gearbox systems.
